Concrete Repair & Resurfacing · Windermere, FL

Concrete Driveway and Slab Repair in Windermere

Concrete repair and resurfacing in Windermere runs $3–$10 per sq ft (resurfacing) as of October 2026. The town's median home dates to 1989, and population growth has stayed modest since 2020, so most cracking here traces to decades of ordinary wear on older slabs rather than fresh settlement on freshly filled lots.

A driveway from Windermere's median build year is pushing 35 years old

Windermere's median year structure built is 1989 Census Reporter, Windermere FL, and the town grew only from 3,159 residents in the 2020 base count to an estimated 3,344 by July 2025 Census Bureau PEP, Vintage 2025, a slower pace than several newer cities in the same unit. Thirty-five summers of expansion and contraction is a lot for one slab to absorb, and once a joint or crack has already been patched once, a second patch rarely lasts as long as simply resurfacing the whole panel would.

Orange County is on the state's sinkhole-claims list, but settlement is still the usual culprit

Orange County is one of the eleven counties the Florida Senate flagged for the heaviest statewide sinkhole insurance claims in a 2010 review Florida Senate Interim Report 2011-104, a different finding than some neighboring counties that didn't make that list. Florida's own geological survey still draws a clear line between a sudden cover-collapse sinkhole and the slower, far more common cover-subsidence kind FDEP/FGS Sinkhole FAQ, and a dip near a 35-year-old Windermere driveway reads far more like ordinary fill settlement than either category of sinkhole.

What's actually missing under a dipped slab

A slab rarely sinks because the concrete itself failed. It sinks because the compacted base underneath lost material, usually washed out by water that found a path through a joint or a crack over several rainy seasons. That missing material leaves a void, and the panel above holds its shape until enough of the void opens up that the concrete settles into the gap. Mudjacking and polyjacking both work by filling that void rather than touching the slab, which is why either method can level a surface without demolition. Figuring out how far the void actually extends under a Windermere driveway, not just where the dip shows on top, decides whether injection is the right fix at all.

Polyjacking moves faster per hole, but needs closer attention

Polyjacking's smaller injection holes and foam that expands within minutes mean a crew works through more injection points in less total time than a comparable mudjacking job, but each one needs closer monitoring since over-injecting foam can lift a slab too far or crack it from underneath. The crew checks the rise after each short injection rather than after a long, continuous pour, adjusting as they go. For a Windermere homeowner comparing quotes, polyjacking's speed per hole is real, but it trades off against a process that leaves less room for a crew to work carelessly and still get away with it.

Patching a driveway built around the town's median year

Say a two-car driveway measuring 460 square feet, poured sometime close to 1989 when the town's typical home went up, has gone chalky and picked up a scatter of narrow surface cracks across both panels. Pricing a resurfacing overlay at $3–$10 per sq ft (resurfacing) comes out to $1,380 through $4,600, settling closer to $1,840 and $3,220 inside the typical $4–$7 band, a fraction of what tearing out and re-pouring the whole slab at the higher $6–$15 per sq ft figure would cost. Which path actually makes sense turns on what the base underneath looks like once a panel or two gets opened up, not on the driveway's age by itself.

The grout mix behind mudjacking, and the foam behind polyjacking

Mudjacking works through small holes, usually about 1 to 2 inches across, drilled in a grid pattern, then a soil-cement-water slurry is pumped under pressure until the slab lifts back to grade. Polyjacking uses smaller holes, closer to 5/8 inch, and injects a two-part polyurethane foam that expands within the void in minutes rather than filling it with liquid grout. Mudjacking nationally runs about $4 to $9 per square foot, polyjacking about $8 to $25, a gap that largely reflects material cost rather than labor. Either method leaves a small patched hole pattern across the Windermere driveway once the job is done.

A replaced panel that never quite matches the rest of the driveway

New concrete and old concrete age differently: the fresh panel starts out a slightly different shade, cures at its own rate, and can take years of sun exposure to weather close to the surrounding slab's color, if it ever fully matches. That's a cosmetic reality of cut-out-and-replace, not a flaw in the work itself, and it's worth setting that expectation with a Windermere homeowner before the job starts rather than after. A mismatched panel that's structurally sound and correctly tied into the joint pattern is a successful repair even while it visibly reads as newer than what's around it.

Sealing hairline cracks before they become a void underneath

A hairline crack that's left alone keeps acting as a path for water to reach the base below, slowly carrying away the fines and sand that hold the slab up, the same process that eventually calls for mudjacking or a cut-out repair. Filling a crack while it's still small, before the next rainy season rather than after, is cheap compared with the injection or replacement work needed once a real void has formed underneath a Windermere driveway. Routine crack sealing is less a cosmetic habit than a way of protecting the base nobody can see.

Frequently asked questions

Should I worry about cracking in an older Windermere driveway?

Usually not right away. With the town's median home dating to 1989, scattered surface cracking and worn control joints are what three and a half decades of Florida sun and rain normally leave behind, not necessarily a sign the slab has failed.

Is Orange County a sinkhole-prone area?

It's among the eleven counties the Florida Senate flagged for the heaviest sinkhole insurance claims statewide in a 2010 review. Even so, the far more common explanation for a sunken slab is ordinary settlement, not either kind of sinkhole the state's geological survey tracks.

Is resurfacing cheaper than full replacement for an older Windermere driveway?

Per square foot, yes, but only when the subgrade under the existing slab is still sound. Once the base itself has shifted, resurfacing tends to crack again within a season or two, so opening up a panel to look is worth more than guessing from the home's age.
